clue.text: Brave opponent, despite his wan appearance

explanation.surface: A warrior faces down his enemy even though he looks pale and drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'brave' is a Native American warrior in old westerns, whose opponent was the white settler; the second sense is a literal pallid face.
explanation.definitionFit: In western fiction the settlers fighting Native American warriors were called this, and a wan look is literally a pallid countenance.

clue.text: A professor with sex appeal has the advantage

parts.note: prof is the short form of professor
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: A charismatic academic has an edge over rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Gain or benefit from something is a synonym of advantage.

clue.text: They throw illumination on the answers crosswords to crosswords

explanation.surface: Something that sheds light on how crossword clues are solved.
explanation.walkthrough: The page as printed repeats 'crosswords'; the clue means 'the answers to crosswords'. Setters call the entries in a grid its lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamps cast illumination, and in crossword jargon each grid entry is called a light.

clue.text: Touch by giving a bit of a hand

explanation.surface: Making contact by lending someone a little help.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel something with the digits is to touch it, and a digit is one part of the hand.

clue.text: Ideal wear when it's cold in an Eastern country

indicators.note: the word for cold is placed inside the name of the country

parts.note: China is a country in East Asia
a chill is coldness

explanation.surface: Advice on what to put on in a frosty Asian land.
explanation.definitionFit: This rodent's soft fur makes a warm, luxurious coat, ideal clothing for cold weather.

clue.text: The sum to be paid for a horse

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: The price someone pays to buy a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A total figure owed is the quantity or sum due.

clue.text: I'm upset by tension in the teaching profession

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the letters of I'm are turned over, read upwards

parts.note: stress is strain or tension

explanation.surface: A teacher frets about the strain of working in schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns I'm into MI, which STRESS follows. The definition is descriptive: a schoolmistress works in teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmistress is a female teacher, so she belongs to the teaching profession.

clue.text: Have breakdowns in a University friend been caused by vie lent change?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for friend

parts.note: pal is an informal word for friend

indicators.note: a breakdown here means the word Have is broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Asks whether a college friend's collapses came from some drastic turn of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakdowns' scrambles HAVE into HEAV, which 'in' places inside PAL, after U.
explanation.definitionFit: An upheaval is a sudden, disruptive transformation or upset.

clue.text: Teach a group of schoolchildren to make a model railway

parts.note: to train someone is to teach them
a set is a class of pupils grouped by ability

explanation.surface: Getting a class to build a toy railway layout.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy locomotive with carriages and track sold as a kit is a miniature railway.

clue.text: Appeal to be given new reading material

parts.note: O is the interjection of appeal, as in 'O Lord'

indicators.note: new means the letters of the next word are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A plea to be handed fresh books to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges READING into RGANDIE, after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiff muslin fabric, a type of cloth.

clue.text: A way the headmaster receives a complaint

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
HM is the abbreviation for headmaster

explanation.surface: A head teacher on some road is handed a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' here is an illness, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be a medical ailment, and this breathing disorder is one.

clue.text: Where to catch the player red handed

definitions.text: Where to catch the player red handed

parts.words: Where to catch the player red handed
parts.note: a player performs in an act on stage, and someone caught red-handed is caught mid-deed

explanation.surface: Where you might nab an actor caught doing wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching someone during a misdeed is catching them red-handed, and a performer appears within a theatrical turn.

clue.text: Arrange radio broadcast before noon

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of radio are spread out anew

explanation.surface: Scheduling a radio programme for the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns RADIO into ORDAI, which comes before N.
explanation.definitionFit: To decree or order something is to arrange it by authority.

clue.text: Risk going to sea if it's in one's own interest!

indicators.note: going to means the word for risk is attached after the word for sea

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
a chance is a gamble or risk

explanation.surface: Taking a gamble on a sea voyage if it pays you personally.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an eye to the main chance means pursuing personal advantage.

clue.text: The last coach on the last lap

parts.note: final means last
a stage is a stagecoach

explanation.surface: The final carriage on the closing circuit of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing phase of a race or process is its concluding leg.

clue.text: Bill and I have depression as the result of car crash

parts.note: acc is the abbreviation for account, a bill
a dent is a hollow or depression

explanation.surface: A billing mishap and a dented car after a collision.
explanation.definitionFit: A road collision is an unplanned mishap.

clue.text: Expert discovered to be possessed of great depth

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
found means discovered

explanation.surface: A specialist turns out to be deeply thoughtful.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep, whether of water or of thought, is a synonym here.

clue.text: Nightingale in Tuscany

explanation.surface: A songbird singing in central Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence Nightingale was the nursing pioneer, and the city is the capital of Tuscany.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursing pioneer's first name, and also the Italian city on the Arno in Tuscany.

clue.text: Two geometrical features in the London Underground

parts.note: a circle is a basic shape in geometry
a line is another basic element of geometry

explanation.surface: Shapes spotted on the Tube map.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a route on the London Tube; the definition says it is found there.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the routes of London's Tube network, running in a loop round the centre.

clue.text: Cancer, for example, is a subject Rex is immersed in

indicators.note: the king's letter is plunged inside the word for subject

parts.note: a topic is a subject
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king steeped in the subject of disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cancer' suggests the disease; it is the Tropic of Cancer, a line of latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Cancer names one of the two latitude lines bounding the torrid zone.

clue.text: Contemptible fellow in American intelligence bureau is a chirpy little thing!

indicators.note: the fellow goes inside the agency's letters

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A rotter working for US spies is a cheery little chap.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect makes a loud chirping noise.

clue.text: Witness the situation of cricket fans

explanation.surface: Watching where cricket supporters are.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, at Test: fans are at the Test match, cricket's international game.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness is to vouch for something; spectators watching a Test match are at the Test.

clue.text: Popular company, but ailing

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A well-liked business that is nonetheless struggling.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail or weak through age or illness, like sick.

clue.text: Old political reformer is a church painter

parts.note: a painter is an artist

explanation.surface: A Victorian activist who decorates churches.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chartists were a 19th-century British movement demanding votes for working men.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the 1830s-40s People's Charter campaign sought parliamentary reform.

clue.text: Queen resolved to take in one of the horses

indicators.note: the rearranged letters enclose the letter for one
resolved here means broken down and reworked, so the letters of Queen are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The monarch decided to adopt one of the horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges QUEEN as EQUNE, which takes in I.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective means relating to the horse family.

clue.text: Where food is served without effort

explanation.surface: A meal dished up with no trouble at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner arrives on crockery, and the idiom for something handed over easily uses the same phrase.

clue.text: More in order for Diana to be placed in the middle of the row

indicators.text: to be placed in the middle of
indicators.note: Di is put inside the word for row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
Di is the short form of Diana

explanation.surface: Diana is seated in the centre of the row.
explanation.definitionFit: Neater, more orderly is the comparative of neat.

clue.text: Strong inclination to write a song

parts.note: to pen is to write
a chant is a simple song

explanation.surface: A keen urge to compose music.
explanation.definitionFit: A liking or fondness for something.
